item.title: What records reveal about Newsom's taxpayer-funded, California-branded free diaper program
item.description: CBS California Investigates reviewed 356 pages of state records behind California's $6.2 million diaper contract with Baby2Baby. Here is what they show.

item.title: Dr. Deborah Birx on combative Fauci hearing: "We have to have a better way forward than this"
item.description: Former White House Coronavirus Response Coordinator Dr. Deborah Birx worked, in her words, in the trenches with Dr. Anthony Fauci during the COVID-19 pandemic. Birx joins "The Takeout" with her thoughts on Fauci's diaries, his actions during the pandemic and the debate over COVID's origins.

item.title: Salman Rushdie attacker convicted in federal trial over 2022 stabbing
item.description: A man has been convicted of federal terrorism charges in the 2022 stabbing of author Salman Rushdie.

item.title: Fed holds interest rates steady, but 3 officials vote for hike
item.description: Fed officials are leaving their benchmark rate unchanged for a fifth straight meeting, a sign they expect inflation to ease.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy trial jury hears ex-husband's 911 call after murders
item.description: Lindsay Clancy is standing trial on charges that she murdered her three young children in Duxbury, Massachusetts, in 2023.

item.title: Sen. Rand Paul says there's a "very real chance" Fauci could be prosecuted after contentious hearing
item.description: Dr. Anthony Fauci repeatedly invoked the Fifth Amendment during a Senate hearing about the COVID-19 pandemic on Wednesday, angering Republican lawmakers. GOP Sen. Rand Paul of Kentucky, who led the hearing, joins "The Takeout" with his reaction.

item.title: Elephants that died in Kenya likely poisoned by cyanide-tainted tomatoes
item.description: Fifteen elephants in southern Kenya are suspected to have been poisoned by cyanide-contaminated tomatoes, according to wildlife authorities.

item.title: FTC sues Hims & Hers, alleging it shared health data with Meta, Snap
item.description: Telehealth platform disclosed users' "most private" health info and locked consumers into subscriptions, regulators allege.

item.title: Trump-affiliated companies distance themselves from Trump-IRS deal
item.description: Top Senate Democrats sought answers about Trump IRS deal from mining company Kaz Resources, cryptocurrency companies World Liberty Financial and prediction markets Polymarket and Kalshi.

item.title: Trump vows to retaliate after U.S. thwarts Iranian surprise attack
item.description: President Trump on Wednesday threatened to hit Iran "very hard" after the U.S. thwarted a surprise attack targeting forces in the Middle East. CBS News White House reporter Aaron Navarro has the latest.

item.title: Dow closes down over 1,000 points as Fed leaves rates unchanged
item.description: Amid energy price spikes caused by the Iran war and persistently high inflation, the Federal Reserve decided on Wednesday to hold interest rates steady for the fifth straight time. CBS News MoneyWatch correspondent Kelly O'Grady reports.

item.title: Trump warns Iran is set to "get a beating" as 5-month war expands
item.description: The war in the Middle East is expanding, with President Trump threatening Iran with "a beating" and the U.S. and Saudi Arabia jointly striking Iranian proxies in Iraq.

item.title: Trump unveils plans for overhaul of Dulles airport outside Washington
item.description: President Trump said he hopes the renovations will take Dulles from "an impossible airport" to one of the world's best.

item.title: How Trump drafted renovation plans for Dulles, a "terrible airport"
item.description: President Trump asked for 3D models of the renovation proposals as he personally tweaked ideas to overhaul Dulles International Airport that are scheduled to be unveiled on Wednesday.

item.title: Why are airlines banning humanoid robots from flights?
item.description: Three major U.S. airlines have quietly changed their policies to ban humanoid and animal-like robots from their flights.

item.title: Trump asks Supreme Court to overturn $83.3 million E. Jean Carroll case
item.description: President Trump is asking the Supreme Court to throw out an $83.3 million defamation judgment the writer E. Jean Carroll won against him.

item.title: Schools are testing pepper-spraying drones to stop shooters
item.description: Schools in three states will be equipped with drones this coming academic year that aim to find and deter active shooters within seconds.

item.title: Friend describes last known movements of missing American in Grenada
item.description: American Elizabeth Waddell was last seen on July 22 while visiting the tiny Caribbean island of Grenada.

item.title: William Shatner and daughter Melanie recall fighting Stage 4 cancer together
item.description: Actor William Shatner and his daughter, Melanie Shatner Gretsch, recall how they helped each other as they fought Stage 4 cancer side by side.

item.title: North Carolina woman missing in Grenada as husband heads to join search
item.description: Elizabeth "Liz" Waddell was last seen at Grand Anse Beach on Wednesday, July 22, the Royal Grenada Police Force said on social media.

item.title: The Footprint | Post Mortem
item.description: Watch "The Footprint" and then join "48 Hours" host Anne-Marie Green and correspondent Erin Moriarty on "Post Mortem" as they discuss the cold case murder of Jeanie Childs, who was stabbed to death in 1993. Almost three decades later, her killer was finally convicted. They discuss the investigative genetic genealogy that led authorities to Jerry Westrom, a local businessman and father of three, and the bloody footprints left at the crime scene that were pivotal at trial.

item.title: Facing a Monster | Post Mortem
item.description: Watch "Facing a Monster" and then catch up with CBS News correspondent Natalie Morales and "48 Hours" correspondent Anne-Marie Green on "Post Mortem" as they discuss the survivor story of C.C. Opanowski, who was violently attacked by her ex-boyfriend, Shawn Doyle, when she was a teenager in 1996. They examine Doyle's escalating pattern of violence, which ultimately led to the 2005 murder of Lori Leonard, a single mom of two young sons, and how C.C. bravely faced Doyle in court a decade after her assault.

item.title: The Boy Across the Street | Post Mortem
item.description: Watch "The Boy Across the Street " and then join "Post Mortem" host Anne-Marie Green and "48 Hours" correspondent Erin Moriarty as they discuss the 1979 murder of Catina Rose Salarno, who was shot by her ex-boyfriend, Steven Burns, and her family's ongoing fight to keep him in prison. Erin shares how her producers tracked down witnesses more than four decades later, how attending the recent parole hearing changed her opinion on the case, and the lasting impact Salarno's death has had on her family.

item.title: The Farris Wheel | Post Mortem
item.description: The matriarch of a wealthy family spins a tale trying to pin the murder of her husband on her own son. Watch "The Farris Wheel" and then join "Post Mortem" host Anne-Marie Green and "48 Hours" correspondent Peter Van Sant as they discuss the murder of Gary Farris, whose remains were discovered in a burn pile on his farm in 2018. His wife, Melody, was convicted of his murder. They discuss the shocking moment when Melody claimed their son was the killer, the lingering mystery of how Gary's body was moved to the burn pile, and Peter's exclusive interview with Melody right after she was sentenced to life in prison.

item.title: First Love, Then Murder | Post Mortem
item.description: Watch "First Love, Then Murder" and then catch up with host Anne-Marie Green and CBS News correspondent Natalie Morales on "Post Mortem" as they discuss the case of Aaron Friar, who was murdered by Gavin MacFarlane, the boyfriend of Aaron's 15-year-old daughter, Ellie. They examine why police believed Ellie was the mastermind behind her father's killing, the handwritten murder plots they found in Gavin's house, and the video of Gavin's friend, Russell, who was taunting police through cameras in the interrogation room.

item.title: The Day My Mother Never Came Home | Post Mortem
item.description: Host Anne-Marie Green and CBS News National Correspondent Vladimir Duthiers discuss the 1987 murder of Selonia Reed that went unsolved for over thirty years. They discuss how Selonia's son, Reggie Jr., grappled with learning his father, Reginald, was the prime suspect years later, the life insurance policies Reginald took out on Selonia leading up to her death, and the twins with identical DNA who complicated the investigation.

item.title: "Dead Girls Don't Talk" | Post Mortem
item.description: Brave survivors speak out after a man charged with murder for poisoning two women tells a friend, "dead girls don't talk." Join CBS News correspondent Jonathan Vigliotti and "48 Hours" producer Michelle Fanucci on "Post Mortem" as they discuss their latest report on the murders of Christy Giles and Hilda Cabrales, who died after David Pearce drugged them. They discuss the twelve "Jane Does" that came forward to testify against Pearce at trial, the personal connection Jonathan had to the victims, and the Google searches Pearce made prior to his arrest that suggested he was trying to flee to Ukraine.

item.title: Could Angela Prichard Have Been Saved? | Post Mortem
item.description: A woman sought help when she was attacked, stalked and intimidated by her husband. It didn't stop him from killing her. Watch "Could Angela Prichard Have Been Saved?" and then join CBS News correspondent Jonathan Vigliotti and "48 Hours" producer Mead Stone on "Post Mortem" as they discuss the case of Angela Prichard, who was gunned down at her workplace by her estranged husband in Bellevue, Iowa. They discuss the 911 call Angela made in the final moments of her life where she named her killer, the two no-contact orders she had against her husband, Christopher, and why her family believes the police didn't do enough to protect her.

item.title: Cati Blauvelt: Death of a Soldier's Wife | Post Mortem
item.description: "48 Hours" correspondent Peter Van Sant and field producer Kat Teurfs discuss the case against John Blauvelt on "Post Mortem." Blauvelt, a one-time military recruiter, went on the run with his teenage girlfriend after stabbing his wife Cati to death. When U.S. Marshals finally tracked him down six years later, Blauvelt was using a different name and living with a new girlfriend across the country. Watch the team discuss the murder weapon, the pirate tattoo authorities used to identify Blauvelt and the journal where he wrote "I did it."

item.title: The Hit-and-Run Homicide of Davis McClendon | Post Mortem
item.description: "48 Hours" correspondent Anne-Marie Green and producer Josh Yager discuss Davis McClendon's death. McClendon was fatally struck by a truck that belonged to Bud Ackerman, the estranged husband of McClendon's love interest. Watch the "Post Mortem" podcast for more on the defense's argument that the collision was an accident, and discover the digital evidence from Ackerman's truck. Also, find out why the Ackermans' babysitter was the first one on the scene to call 911.
